:::{#def-integral}
#### Integral of a real-valued function

Let $(S, \mathscr{S}, \mu)$ be a [measure space](#def-measure-space),
and let $f : S \to \reals$ be [measurable](#def-measurable-function).
The **positive part** and **negative part** of $f$ are the non-negative functions

$$
\ba
f^{+}(s) &\eqdef \max\cb{f(s), 0} \\
f^{-}(s) &\eqdef \max\cb{-f(s), 0}
\ea
$$

so that $f = f^{+} - f^{-}$ and $\abs{f} = f^{+} + f^{-}$.
The **integral** of $f$ with respect to $\mu$ is

$$\int_S f \, d\mu \eqdef \int_S f^{+} \, d\mu - \int_S f^{-} \, d\mu,$$

using @def-integral-nonneg for each term,
when at least one of the two terms is finite;
otherwise, the integral of $f$ is undefined.
($f^{+}$, $f^{-}$, and $\abs{f}$ are measurable when $f$ is
[@billingsley1995probability, Section 13].)

[@billingsley1995probability, Section 15]

:::
